propositions: Provider qualification currently uses a shape regex (`_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE`) that matches prefix patterns instead of checking membership in a known provider registry, causing typo'd configured providers (e.g. 'bedrok') to be silently accepted at config-resolution time and only caught later at provider construction.

The shape regex incorrectly rejects valid provider names containing slashes (e.g. 'gateway/openai') and would incorrectly accept any future model id whose pre-colon prefix matches the identifier pattern, repeating the defect that issue 03b0 fixed.

Provider qualification must be decided by membership in a static frozenset of 24 known provider names derived from pydantic-ai's registry, matching the design pattern used by LangChain and LiteLLM, without importing optional packages at config resolution time.

An explicitly configured provider must be validated against the known-provider registry and raise LLMConfigError at config-resolution time if unknown; an unrecognized inline prefix in a model string must fall back to unqualified (returning the whole string) to preserve colon-bearing model ids like Bedrock's 'anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0'.

The 'test' and 'google_genai' provider names must be removed from the set despite being pinned by existing tests, as they are not members of pydantic-ai's runtime registries and admitting them makes rebar more permissive than the library it wraps.

A drift test must validate that the static set remains a superset of both pydantic-ai's known providers and rebar's own builders, guarded by importorskip to maintain the stdlib-only property of the config layer.
